docs/research\URI_AGENT_LOOP_ROOT_CAUSE_AUDIT.md:341:**What the model sees.** MCP formalizes tool discovery as an explicit client-server handshake — a client queries what tools a server offers and receives "a machine-readable list of functions... describing each available action, its inputs, and output format" before ever invoking one ([Model Context Protocol specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25); [CodiLime, "Model Context Protocol (MCP) explained"](https://codilime.com/blog/model-context-protocol-explained/)). Anthropic's own engineering guidance is explicit that a tool must be described as if "writing for an alien collaborator who needs every detail spelled out" ([Anthropic, "Writing effective tools for AI agents"](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents)) — URI's M27 registry violates this directly: the *model* is never told the multi-action proposal shape exists at all, which is a strictly worse position than "the tool description is imperfect" (§9, case B).
docs/research\URI_AGENT_LOOP_ROOT_CAUSE_AUDIT.md:345:**How tools are discovered / tool-explosion is avoided.** Both MCP-Zero and ScaleMCP exist specifically because naively injecting every tool's full schema into every prompt does not scale — "this expansion creates significant context overhead, as traditional approaches inject all server JSON-Schemas into system prompts simultaneously" ([MCP-Zero](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.01056); [ScaleMCP](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.06416)). URI's own M27 `CapabilityDiscoveryEngine` already implements the right *shape* of the correct answer here (summaries first, full action schema only after selection) — it is simply never reached (§9, case B), and the legacy path has no progressive-discovery concept at all (every legacy capability name is exposed flatly, unconditionally, every turn).
docs/research\URI_AGENT_LOOP_ROOT_CAUSE_AUDIT.md:347:**How action schemas are scoped.** The same MCP/ScaleMCP sources converge on scoping schemas to relevance rather than dumping the full catalogue. URI has this capability (M27's two-stage discovery) sitting unused beside a legacy path that has no such scoping.
docs/research\URI_AGENT_LOOP_ROOT_CAUSE_AUDIT.md:351:**How unsupported actions are handled.** None of the surveyed systems treat "no tool matches" as an afterthought inferred by exhaustion; MCP's discovery handshake and LangGraph's explicit conditional edges both make "no matching capability" a first-class, examinable state rather than a fallthrough. URI's equivalent (§5, §9 case D) is structurally the weakest point found in this audit: `known_gaps` exists and is even correctly computed, but never reaches the decision step, only the drafting step.
docs/research\URI_AGENT_LOOP_ROOT_CAUSE_AUDIT.md:357:**How weaker models are supported.** Anthropic's context-engineering guidance recommends "just in time" context (lightweight references loaded on demand rather than everything up front) and treating tool responses with "pagination, range selection, filtering... for any tool responses that could use up lots of context" specifically because smaller/weaker models degrade faster under prompt bulk ([Anthropic, "Effective context engineering for AI agents"](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)). `model_reasoning_adapter.py`'s own comments independently rediscovered this exact lesson for qwen3:14b (conditionally-appended prompt addenda, explicitly to avoid "prompt bulk it doesn't need") — this is one place URI's own engineering already matches current best practice, arrived at empirically rather than by design.

## F-C1 decision: Codex session persistence vs resume

Decided from URI's requirements, not convenience:

* URI owns task/intent/execution state; the executor's thread/session id is **resumable execution metadata**. It is
  persisted only on the `attempt` row of the task that produced it (needed for safe continuation), never elsewhere.
* Reuse is bounded to one path: a `RESUME_SESSION` retry of the **same task**, under the **same authorization row**
  (admission re-checks validity, so a revoked or expired authorization blocks the resume), with the **same executor
  registration** (a re-registered executor runs fresh and the refusal is recorded as `attempt.resume_refused`), the
  **same model** (the model travels with the authorized work, never with the session), and a session id that still
  validates (`valid_session_id`, bypass tokens refused).
* Missing, stale or invalid session: Codex answers with a terminal error claim; reconciliation treats it as an ordinary
  failed attempt (`RETRY_FRESH` if budget remains, else `FAILED RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`). It can never produce
  COMPLETE and never bypasses the authority check: fail closed or the governed retry path.
* Settled/completed tasks are never re-admitted; a supervisor restart revokes the authority and fails the leftover
  (Phase 2B rule), so a resumable thread is abandoned after a restart (new ticket required).
* Codex thread persistence in the user's own Codex store: kept (no `--ephemeral`), because resume is a qualified
  capability (Phase 2C real evidence) and URI's correctness never depends on that store (failure = retry path). This is
  the product trade-off recorded in Phase 2C F-C1; the owner may still choose `--ephemeral` later (one spec change).

A record is written only by a trusted qualification run (`phase2d_composition_qualification.py`) and only when the
direct probe succeeded AND the live auth status is ok. On every load (worker start, `harness_discover`) it is
re-validated; any drift invalidates it (reported, never silently inherited):

|---|---|
| executable missing / different file at the path | `EXECUTABLE_MISSING` |
| executable bytes changed (npm `codex.CMD` shim included) | `EXECUTABLE_HASH_MISMATCH`; the bridge also pins the hash at run time (`EXECUTOR_BINARY_HASH_MISMATCH`, no task) |
| `--version` differs | `VERSION_MISMATCH` |
| record edited by hand | `RECORD_DIGEST_MISMATCH` (file unreadable / wrong schema: `RECORD_UNREADABLE` / `RECORD_SCHEMA`) |
| `FIXTURE_ONLY` record in a production profile | `LEVEL_NOT_ALLOWED` (only `--allow-fixture-qualification`, test profile) |
| provider refused/unknown (Antigravity) | `PROVIDER_REFUSED_OR_UNKNOWN` |
| model not in the record's `models` | bridge `NOT_STARTED:MODEL_NOT_QUALIFIED` before any task |
| authentication | never persisted; live probe each time (`AUTHENTICATED` / `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` / `AUTH_UNVERIFIED`), usable only when `AUTHENTICATED` |

Codex is **not** URI's permanent Main Brain: it is one qualified `(provider, executable, model)` row the server may
offer and the client may run; the deterministic row is always offered; click-to-choose selection is unchanged.

* The UI remains outside authority: it sends `turn_start`, `turn_intent` (digest-bound confirm/abandon/select) and

"""Phase 2D worker-side service: the frozen worker protocol, served by the SupervisedTurnRunner.

Same commands and envelopes as the frozen `TurnService` (`turn_start`, `turn_intent`, `turn_decide`), so the
frozen UI client (`uri_ui/lib/services/paired_runtime.dart`) could drive it unchanged, plus two strict additions:

  * `turn_decide` MAY carry `approval_digest`: when present it must equal the digest of the approval request the
    worker showed for that turn; a mismatch drops the pending turn and refuses (`APPROVAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH`). A UI
    that echoes the digest it displayed therefore cannot approve a turn whose arguments changed underneath it. The
    worker still binds the approval to its own pending record either way (UI is never the authority).
  * `turn_cancel {turn_id}`: explicit withdrawal of a pending (not yet dispatched) turn. It is sent to the server as
    a denial, so nothing is ever executed for it. There is no mid-run cancel over this single-threaded protocol;
    the bridge's `cancel()` exists for an owning composition that runs the worker loop in a thread, and worker death
    propagates through the kill-on-close job (Phase 2A/2C evidence).

Pending state is memory-only, exactly as in the frozen service: a worker restart or reconnect drops every pending
turn (fail closed, `TURN_NOT_PENDING`), and the frozen server's own guards (`INTENT_EXECUTION_UNCERTAIN`,
`INTENT_ALREADY_EXECUTED`, duplicate operation ids) prevent a second execution of the same work.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from uri_core.client_runtime.turn_runner import TurnError

from .runner import SupervisedTurnService

COMMAND_SCHEMAS = {
    "turn_start": ({"command", "session_id", "text", "reasoning"},),
    "turn_intent": ({"command", "session_id", "text", "reasoning", "intent_decision"},),
    "turn_decide": ({"command", "turn_id", "approve"}, {"command", "turn_id", "approve", "approval_digest"}),
    "turn_cancel": ({"command", "turn_id"},),
}


class SupervisedWorkerService(SupervisedTurnService):
    def handle(self, kind, command):
        shapes = COMMAND_SCHEMAS.get(kind)
        if shapes is None or set(command) not in shapes:
            raise TurnError("COMMAND_SCHEMA")
        if kind == "turn_cancel":
            entry = self.pending.pop(command["turn_id"], None)
            if entry is None:
                raise TurnError("TURN_NOT_PENDING")
            text, session, reasoning, turn = entry
            return self._public(self._runner().decide(text, session, reasoning, turn, False))
        if kind == "turn_decide":
            turn_id = command["turn_id"]
            if not isinstance(turn_id, str) or not isinstance(command["approve"], bool):
                self.pending.pop(turn_id, None) if isinstance(turn_id, str) else None
                raise TurnError("TURN_NOT_PENDING")
            if "approval_digest" in command:
                entry = self.pending.get(turn_id)
                shown = ((entry[3].get("approval_request") or {}).get("approval_digest")) if entry else None
                if entry is None or not isinstance(command["approval_digest"], str) or command["approval_digest"] != shown:
                    self.pending.pop(turn_id, None)
                    raise TurnError("APPROVAL_DIGEST_MISMATCH" if entry is not None else "TURN_NOT_PENDING")
                command = {k: v for k, v in command.items() if k != "approval_digest"}
        return super().handle(kind, command)
"""Phase 2D opt-in client worker: the frozen C3 worker protocol with harness execution through the supervisor.

This is a COMPOSITION PROFILE, not a cutover: the frozen `scripts/run_uri_client_worker.py` stays the entrypoint named
by every client manifest and the one the frozen UI spawns. This script accepts the same manifest, applies the same
C1 gates (isolated mode, bootstrap import gate, source pin, cwd, sanitized environment, fixture guard, single
instance, key/image identity), and differs only in what it composes:

  * `uri_supervisor_bridge.qualification.compose_client`: persisted, re-validated qualification records instead of
    "nothing qualified"; `harness_discover` additionally returns the qualification report;
  * `uri_supervisor_bridge.worker_service.SupervisedWorkerService`: the frozen turn protocol served by the
    `SupervisedTurnRunner` (verify_authority -> SupervisorBridge -> uri_supervisor), plus `turn_cancel` and the
    optional digest-bound `turn_decide`.

`--allow-fixture-qualification` honours `FIXTURE_ONLY` records (test fixture executors); it is never set by a launcher.
Nothing here logs in, reads or copies credentials, or changes any configuration.

c1_bootstrap.__file__, c1_bootstrap.SOURCE = str(_C1_BOOT), _C1_BOOT.read_bytes()

PHASE2_PACKAGES = ("uri_supervisor", "uri_supervisor_bridge")


class Phase2SourceFinder:
    """Same discipline as the C1 bootstrap finder for the two Phase 2 packages: plain source files under the source
    root only, never cached bytecode, digest of the executed bytes recorded. The source root stays off sys.path."""

    def __init__(self, root):
        self.root = os.path.abspath(root)
        self.executed = {}

    def find_spec(self, fullname, path=None, target=None):
        if fullname.partition(".")[0] not in PHASE2_PACKAGES:
            return None
        base = os.path.join(self.root, *fullname.split("."))
        package, module = os.path.join(base, "__init__.py"), base + ".py"
        is_package, is_module = os.path.isfile(package), os.path.isfile(module)
        if is_package and is_module:
            raise ImportError("PHASE2_SOURCE_AMBIGUOUS", name=fullname)
        if not (is_package or is_module):
            raise ImportError("PHASE2_SOURCE_NOT_FOUND", name=fullname)
        origin = package if is_package else module
        loader = c1_bootstrap.SourceOnlyLoader(fullname, origin)
        spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(fullname, origin, loader=loader,
                                                      submodule_search_locations=[base] if is_package else None)
        self.executed[os.path.relpath(origin, self.root).replace("\\", "/")] = loader
        return spec


_ROOT = _C1_BOOT.parents[1]
_P2 = Phase2SourceFinder(_ROOT)

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey  # noqa: E402

def phase2_source_digests():
    """SHA-256 of every Phase 2 source file as it was COMPILED by this process (loader-recorded), for the instance record."""
    out = {}
    for rel, loader in sorted(_P2.executed.items()):
        out[rel] = loader.executed_digest
    return out


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--manifest", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--allow-fixture-qualification", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        manifest = ClientManifest(args.manifest)
        m = manifest.data
        root = Path(m["client_root"])
        install_source_pin(Path(m["source_root"]).resolve(), manifest.source_files)
        if Path.cwd().resolve() != root:
            raise RuntimeIdentityError("CLIENT_CWD_MISMATCH")
        safe = child_environment(root, Path(m["interpreter"]))
        os.environ.clear()
        os.environ.update(safe)
        # Persisted qualification is re-validated under the client-profile environment BEFORE the fixture guard, so
        # the executable hashes and version/auth probes run once here; the guard then admits exactly those files.
        composition, bridge = compose_and_build(root, allow_fixture=args.allow_fixture_qualification)
        from types import SimpleNamespace
        guard = FixtureGuard(SimpleNamespace(data={"state_root": str(root), "source_root": m["source_root"]}))
        for pkg in PHASE2_PACKAGES:
            guard.read_roots.append((Path(m["source_root"]) / pkg).resolve())
        for b in composition.executors.values():
            for p in (b.resolved_executable, *b.extra_argv):
                if p and Path(str(p)).is_file():
                    guard.read_files.add(Path(str(p)).resolve())
        sys.addaudithook(guard)
        with NamedMutex("Local\\URI_Client_" + m["client_id"], 0):
            key = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(dpapi((root / "secure/client-key.dpapi").read_bytes(), True))
            from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
            public = key.public_key().public_bytes(serialization.Encoding.Raw, serialization.PublicFormat.Raw).hex()
            if public != m["client_public_key"]:
                raise RuntimeIdentityError("CLIENT_KEY_MISMATCH")
            from uri_core.client_runtime.persistence import ClientPersistence, PersistenceError
            from uri_core.client_runtime.transport import TransportError
            from uri_core.core.client_state_ports import StatePortError
            from uri_core.client_runtime.turn_runner import TurnError
            persistence = ClientPersistence(manifest)
            import psutil
            process = psutil.Process()
            if Path(process.exe()).resolve() != Path(m["process_image"]).resolve():
                raise RuntimeIdentityError("CLIENT_PROCESS_IMAGE")
            generation = str(uuid.uuid4())
            atomic_json(root / "control/worker-instance.json", {"pid": process.pid,
                "create_time": process.create_time(), "generation": generation, "profile": "phase2d-supervised",
                "client_id": m["client_id"], "manifest_digest": manifest.digest,
                "phase2_source_digest": hashlib.sha256(canonical(phase2_source_digests())).hexdigest(),
                "qualified": composition.qualified(), "fixture_allowed": bool(args.allow_fixture_qualification)})
            guard.starting = False
            harnesses = composition.registry
            turns = SupervisedWorkerService(manifest, persistence, bridge, harness=harnesses)
            while True:
                command = read_frame(sys.stdin.buffer)
                if command is None:
                    break
                try:
                    kind = command.get("command")
                    required = {"identity": {"command", "nonce"}, "snapshot": {"command", "session_id", "queries"},
                                "consent": {"command", "mutations"}, "commit": {"command", "mutations"},
                                "close": {"command"}, "session": {"command"}, "preflight": {"command"},
                                "server_request": {"command", "method", "path", "body"},
                                "harness_discover": {"command"},
                                "turn_start": {"command", "session_id", "text", "reasoning"},
                                "turn_intent": {"command", "session_id", "text", "reasoning", "intent_decision"},
                                "turn_decide": {"command", "turn_id", "approve"},
                                "turn_cancel": {"command", "turn_id"}}
                    if kind not in required or not (set(command) == required[kind]
                                                    or (kind == "turn_decide" and set(command) == required[kind] | {"approval_digest"})):
                        raise ValueError("COMMAND_SCHEMA")
                    if kind == "identity":
                        nonce = command["nonce"]
                        if not isinstance(nonce, str) or len(nonce) != 64 or any(c not in "0123456789abcdef" for c in nonce):
                            raise ValueError("NONCE_INVALID")
                        identity = {"client_id": m["client_id"], "server_id": m["server_id"],
                            "manifest_digest": manifest.digest, "generation": generation, "pid": process.pid,
                            "create_time": process.create_time(), "nonce": nonce}
                        result = {**identity, "signature": key.sign(canonical(identity)).hex()}
                    elif kind == "preflight":
                        from uri_core.client_runtime.readiness import client_preflight
                        result = {**client_preflight(manifest), "worker_profile": "phase2d-supervised",
                                  "production_cutover": False}
                    elif kind == "snapshot":
                        result = persistence.snapshot(command["session_id"], [ReadQuery.model_validate(q) for q in command["queries"]]).model_dump()
                    elif kind in {"consent", "commit"}:
                        mutation_set = ClientMutationSet.model_validate(command["mutations"])
                        if kind == "consent":
                            persistence.consent(mutation_set)
                            result = {"state": "CONSENT_RECORDED"}
                        else:
                            result = persistence.commit(mutation_set)
                    elif kind == "harness_discover":
                        result = {"harnesses": harnesses.discover(), "fallback": "none",
                                  "qualification": composition.report, "supervisor": "uri_supervisor_bridge"}
                    elif kind in {"turn_start", "turn_intent", "turn_decide", "turn_cancel"}:
                        result = turns.handle(kind, command)
                    elif kind in {"session", "server_request"}:
                        from uri_core.client_runtime.transport import ClientTransport
                        transport = ClientTransport(manifest)
                        if kind == "session":
                            result = transport.session()
                        else:
                            if command["method"] not in {"GET", "POST"}:
                                raise ValueError("METHOD_INVALID")
                            result = transport.request(command["method"], command["path"], command["body"])
                    else:
                        write_frame(sys.stdout.buffer, {"result": "CLOSED"})
                        break
                    write_frame(sys.stdout.buffer, {"result": "OK", "value": result})
                except (PersistenceError, TransportError, StatePortError, RuntimeIdentityError, TurnError) as error:
                    write_frame(sys.stdout.buffer, {"result": "REFUSED", "code": str(getattr(error, "code", error))})
                except Exception:
                    write_frame(sys.stdout.buffer, {"result": "REFUSED", "code": "CLIENT_COMMAND_REFUSED"})
            bridge.close()
        return 0
    except Exception:
        print("CLIENT_WORKER_REFUSED", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# URI Harness / Runtime Consumption Strategy: Research Index

**Type:** strategic architecture research. **Not** authorisation to implement, install, migrate, integrate or refactor.
**Date:** 2026-09-27.
**Author role:** Claude Code (Architect / Strategic Researcher, AO-4).
**Checkouts inspected:** `_V1` linked worktree (branch `m35-uri-v1-parallel-architecture`, HEAD `d1feaf7`) and the main worktree `C:\Users\cheta\Development\uri-agent` (`master`, HEAD `e8e3b65`, with uncommitted changes). These are one git repository. The older prototype `E:\Chetan\Uri Agent\uri_prototype` named in `hermes_uri_inventory.json` is not accessible on this machine.
**External primary evidence:**
- Local read-only source of Hermes Agent 0.21.2 at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent` (MIT, commit `284d220`, 2026-09-11).
- Official documentation, repositories and specifications fetched 2026-09-27. URLs are listed in `01`.

**Verdict:** `STRATEGIC_DIRECTION_SUPPORTED_WITH_MAJOR_CONSTRAINTS`

## Primary question and answer

*What should URI own, what should it consume, how should it control consumed systems, and what architecture supports URI Office now and future variants later?*

**Own:**
- the relationship (identity, continuity, knowledge)
- meaning (RAR / ARN / clarification / consequence-aware binding)
- authority (grants, effect classes, approvals, per-harness postures)
- truth (provenance, result versions, **independent outcome verification**)
- economy (Edge ladder, shared model residency, configure-once intelligence brokering)
- stewardship (engine lifecycle)
- domain packs

**Consume:**
- agentic execution, from qualified harnesses behind a URI provider port
- browser, desktop and Office automation, from MCP servers and harness tools
- models, from local servers and cloud providers behind URI's router
- open protocols (ACP, MCP, OpenTelemetry GenAI)

**Control** through:
- outcome-level Execution Capsules
- URI-generated harness profiles
- a URI MCP capability broker for consequential effects
- per-harness authority postures (P0 to P3) earned through qualification
- independent verification

**Architecture:** outcome D (hybrid) with A (URI control plane) at its centre. See `05`.

## User decisions recorded in this investigation

- **D-A.** Codex app-server, Claude Agent SDK and Gemini CLI may be evaluated as execution-harness candidates. Any adoption requires a separate explicit user ruling, because it is in tension with the M31 rule that these development agents must never serve as URI's Brain (`docs/plans/M31_MODEL_BRAIN_UX_PLAN.md:80-82`).
- **D-B.** Authority posture for consequential actions is decided per harness from qualification evidence.
- **D-C.** Treatment of harness-internal memory and self-created skills: the study documents the trade-offs, and the ruling is deferred until experiment E-P10.

## Document map

| # | Document | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | `01_ECOSYSTEM_RESEARCH_REPORT.md` | Ecosystem research (16 areas, primary sources, confidence labels) |
| 02 | `02_CAPABILITY_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX.md` | KEEP / ADAPT / WRAP / REPLACE / BUILD / DEFER per capability |
| 03 | `03_HARNESS_RUNTIME_COMPARISON.md` | Harness comparison (13 candidates) and authority-posture qualification criteria |
| 04 | `04_BRICK_WALL_RISK_REGISTER.md` | Risks and falsification attempt |
| 05 | `05_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md` | Proposed target architecture |
| 06 | `06_PROVIDER_BOUNDARY_PROPOSAL.md` | Minimum HarnessProvider boundary (not frozen) |
| 07 | `07_INTELLIGENCE_SHARING_ANALYSIS.md` | Configure-once intelligence sharing |
| 08 | `08_EXPERIMENT_ROADMAP.md` | NO-PC and PC-REQUIRED experiments (none authorised) |
| 09 | `09_MIGRATION_EVOLUTION_STRATEGY.md` | Staged evolution, reuse and retirement, stale-document findings |
| 10 | `10_STRATEGIC_VISION.md` | Concise vision |

## Why "with major constraints"

The wrapper strategy survived a deliberate falsification attempt (`04` Â§E), but only under these constraints:

1. **Authority is not portable by default.** Hermes approvals are scoped by its own classifier. Its `pre_tool_call` hook fails open on exception. ACP permission requests are issued only when the agent chooses to ask. Consequential effects must go through a URI broker until a harness proves complete, fail-closed interception (posture P3).
2. **Local resources are the binding limit.** Hermes needs a context of at least 64k tokens. The measured 9B residency (5.63 GB weights plus about 1.80 GB KV at 16k context) and the observed 21.7 GB host RAM peak leave uncertain headroom. Fully local harness runs are UNMEASURED and may need a cloud Capable Brain.
3. **No ecosystem verifier exists.** URI must build independent outcome verification. Without it, delegation would reduce URI to trusting "done".
4. **Churn is high.** Weekly or daily harness releases, a breaking MCP revision (2026-07-28) and a supply-chain incident (LiteLLM, March 2026) require pinning, conformance testing and staged upgrades.

# 10 â€” Strategic Vision: URI Core â†’ URI Office â†’ future URI versions

## The one-sentence identity

**URI is the persistent, trustworthy companion that understands what the user means, decides what may happen, hands the work to the best available engine, and proves the result. The engines underneath are replaceable.**

## What URI owns (evidence-based)

Commodity execution is available externally: agent loops, browsers, terminals, computer use, and tool ecosystems. Research found **no external equivalent** for the following, so this is what stays uniquely URI's:

1. **The relationship.** Identity, continuity, persona, preferences and durable knowledge that survive any engine change.
2. **Meaning.** Semantic and reference resolution (RAR), narrowing and clarification (ARN), and consequence-aware binding. No harness binds references authoritatively or knows when a guess is dangerous.
3. **Authority.** Permissions, grants, effect classes, single-use argument-bound approvals, fail-closed boundaries, and per-harness authority postures. Harness approval systems cover only what each harness itself classifies.
4. **Truth.** Provenance, evidence, result versions, and **independent outcome verification**. Every harness reports its own success. None verifies the end state independently.
5. **Economy.** The Edge ladder (deterministic â†’ Edge â†’ Capable â†’ harness), shared model residency, and configure-once intelligence brokering. Harnesses send everything to one large model.
6. **Stewardship.** Engine discovery, pinning, qualification, upgrade approval, rollback and replacement, so the user never manages a second product.
7. **Domain understanding**, packaged as domain packs.

## What URI consumes

- Agentic execution: qualified harnesses behind a URI provider port, preferring open, local-endpoint-capable, Windows-native candidates.
- Browser, desktop and Office automation: MCP servers and harness-native tools, each qualified.
- Models: local servers and cloud providers behind URI's router.
- Protocols: ACP to drive agents, MCP to offer and consume tools, OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions for traces. A2A and AG-UI are deferred until needed.

## Product line

```
URI Core   â€” domain-neutral control plane (relationship, meaning, authority, truth, economy, stewardship)
  â””â”€ URI Office (first domain pack)
       documents Â· spreadsheets Â· presentations Â· PDFs Â· email Â· files Â· browser & portal workflows
       Â· scripts Â· verification of completed office work
  â””â”€ future packs (not designed now): Content/Creator Â· Personal Â· Health/Diet Â· ...
```

A domain pack declares:
- capability exposure
- vocabulary
- rules
- workflow hints
- verifiers
- default policies
- harness profile templates

It never modifies Core authority. Future packs will be possible if one discipline starts now: **no new Office-specific logic enters `uri_core/core/`**.

## How it should feel (URI Office)

- **Bounded requests** ("find last week's circular", "draft the noting") answer immediately through deterministic and Edge paths. No heavyweight engine starts.
- **Open-ended requests** ("make this script work with this spreadsheet") produce a visible plan. URI then starts a qualified engine that the user can watch. Consequential steps pause for URI approval. URI verifies the result and shows the evidence. It says "verified", or it says exactly what it could not verify.
- **The user never configures Hermes, Codex or any other engine.** URI asks only about things that matter: cost, privacy, permissions, and consequential upgrades.

## Constraints this vision accepts (from evidence)

- Fully local agentic execution on a 16 GB GPU is **unproven**. Harness runs may need a cloud Capable Brain, with user awareness, until experiments show otherwise.
- Authority over harness actions must be **earned per harness**. Until it is proven, external effects flow only through URI's broker.
- The ecosystem moves weekly. URI's stability comes from its own boundaries, not from any engine's.

def raw(db):

    try:
        return con
    except Exception:

def test_simulated_abrupt_termination_keeps_every_committed_fact_and_recovers(tmp_path, point):
    cfg, target = cfg_for(tmp_path, scenario="ok_write")
    if point.startswith("recovery_"):
        r = child(cfg, crash_at="after_attempt_ended")
        assert r.returncode == 137, r.stderr[-500:]
        r = child({**cfg, "mode": "recover"}, crash_at=point)
    else:
        r = child(cfg, crash_at=point)
    assert r.returncode == 137, (point, r.stderr[-800:])
    db = Path(cfg["db"])
    # (b) acknowledged commits present, read through a fresh read-only connection (no supervisor, no recovery)
    con = raw(db)
    try:
        for sql in COMMITTED[point]:
            assert con.execute(sql).fetchone()[0] >= 1, (point, sql)
        # (c) structural integrity of what is on disk
        assert con.execute("PRAGMA integrity_check").fetchone()[0] == "ok"
        wal_mode = con.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode").fetchone()[0].lower()
        assert wal_mode == "wal"
    finally:
        con.close()
    # (a) durability settings in force on the next writer; (d) recovery decides and invariants hold
    sup = Supervisor(db)
    try:
        rep = sup.ledger.durability_report()
        assert rep["journal_mode"] == "wal" and rep["synchronous"] == "FULL", rep
        L = sup.ledger
        invariants(L)
        for a in L.q("SELECT attempt_id,task_id,status FROM attempt"):
            assert a["status"] in ("ENDED", "FENCED")
            assert L.q1("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM recovery_decision WHERE attempt_id=?", (a["attempt_id"],))[0] == 1
        assert L.q1("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM task WHERE state IN ('RUNNING','RECOVERING')")[0] == 0
        assert L.q1("PRAGMA integrity_check")[0] == "ok"
    finally:
        sup.close()
    # idempotence: a second restart changes no decision
    before = [tuple(r) for r in sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db}?mode=ro", uri=True).execute("SELECT decision_id,outcome,action FROM recovery_decision")]
    sup = Supervisor(db)
    try:
        after = [tuple(r) for r in sup.ledger.q("SELECT decision_id,outcome,action FROM recovery_decision")]
        assert before == after
    finally:
        sup.close()


def test_ledger_refuses_to_run_without_full_durability(tmp_path):
    """The configuration claim is enforced, not assumed: a connection that cannot set FULL/WAL is refused."""
    from uri_supervisor.ledger import Ledger, LedgerError
    import uri_supervisor.ledger as mod
    db = tmp_path / "l" / "ledger.db"
    L = Ledger(db)
    assert L.durability_report()["synchronous"] == "FULL"
    L.close()
    real = sqlite3.connect

    class Conn:
        def __init__(self, c):
            self.c = c

        def execute(self, sql, *a):
            if sql.strip().upper().startswith("PRAGMA SYNCHRONOUS=FULL"):
                return self.c.execute("PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL")
            return self.c.execute(sql, *a)

        def __getattr__(self, name):
            return getattr(self.c, name)

    mod.sqlite3.connect = lambda *a, **k: Conn(real(*a, **k))
    try:
        with pytest.raises(LedgerError):
            Ledger(db)
    finally:
        mod.sqlite3.connect = real

## 4â€“5. Component responsibilities and the deterministic/AI boundary

The deterministic core owns identity, permissions, user mode, explicit selection, source provenance, candidate IDs, resource admission, action consequences, validation, confirmation, execution, persistence, and audit. It may complete bounded work whose correctness is established by rules and grounded data.

Models may interpret, reason, draft, choose among *offered* tools, and propose bindings. Their output remains an untrusted proposal. A modelâ€™s confidence cannot turn a candidate into a verified identity or expand action authority. This follows [ADR-018](C:/Users/cheta/Development/Uri/_V1/URI_Model_Centric_Architecture_Docs/URI_ADR_018_MODEL_CENTRIC_ARCHITECTURE.md) and the [operating policy](C:/Users/cheta/Development/Uri/_V1/URI_Model_Centric_Architecture_Docs/URI_AI_OPERATING_POLICY.md).

**Architectural correction to the initial sketch:** a universal Step-1 semantic decoder would impose latency and reproduce an experimentally weak seam. Semantic interpretation belongs in the cheapest *qualified* route that actually needs it. A capable model can receive a bounded grounded context directly.

## 6. Edge Brain and specialists

A distinct **logical Edge layer** is useful: it gives routine, bounded intelligence a contract, resource budget, and qualification boundary independent of the Capable Brain. It should be a replaceable collection of roles, not a promise that one tiny model can handle them all. Approximately **<1B** remains the strong product target, not a license to broaden Edge work when a larger model happens to score better.

Every proposed role needs the same contract: task and modality envelope; grounded input and source IDs; constrained output or abstention; versioned model, prompt and schema; measured failure and calibration; resource ceiling; escalation rule; and a held-out benchmark against deterministic and Capable Brain baselines.

| Role | Residual problem and proposed boundary | Present conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Reflex tool choice / record extraction | Simple competing-tool or structured-record cases that rules cannot reliably distinguish. Output is a proposed offered capability/record, validated by runtime. | Narrow Needle 3 evidence exists; production integration does not. |
| Argument extraction | Bounded slots from an already understood request; missing or conflicting slots cause abstention. | Needle result 2/4 is insufficient. Test only a newly defined residual class. |
| Clarification rendering | Explain grounded candidate differences when a short deterministic question is inadequate. It cannot create options or IDs. | **UNMEASURED**; simple wording needs no model. |
| Retrieval interpretation / ranking | Compare authorized, grounded candidates when names and metadata are insufficient. Return evidence and uncertainty. | **UNMEASURED**; Graphify hints cannot supply truth. |
| Bounded drafting | Only a precisely defined, low-consequence task class in Auto mode; assess result quality as well as execution. | **UNMEASURED**. Explicitly selected Capable Brain authors substantive drafts, even short ones. |
| OCR, speech, vision and embeddings | Add a modality or retrieval capability only for a measured residual need. Output carries provenance and uncertainty. | No current general Edge qualification. Load on demand if eventually qualified. |

This challenges an easy but costly interpretation of â€œEdge firstâ€: trying Edge on every request would add double inference, errors, and escalation. Edge is **first-class in the route policy**, not mandatory first execution.

## 7. Capable and cloud Brains

The local Capable Brain handles meaningful reasoning, synthesis, substantive drafting, uncertain judgment, multi-step work, and complex tool use. In Auto mode, URI selects the least costly qualified local or authorized cloud route expected to finish reliably. An explicitly selected model is the preferred author of substantive work; Edge may perform qualified supporting steps.

URIâ€™s harness should offer the stronger model native tools and context appropriate to its provider: iterative and parallel tool calls, structured output, multimodal input, and agentic continuation where supported. The model still crosses the same runtime authority boundary. The accepted [M33.2 architecture](C:/Users/cheta/Development/Uri/_V1/docs/architecture/M33_2_EDGE_SECOND_BRAIN_CANONICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md) already distinguishes Edge, hybrid, and Main-preferred behavior; the proposed **local-only / Auto / selected-provider** product control needs a versioned mapping to those existing settings, not an unexplained second policy system.

Auto cloud escalation needs an already connected, user-authorized provider and a visible route trace. It does not authorize email sending, form submission, deletion, or any other external action. In local-only mode, URI reports a limitation or offers a local route rather than silently using cloud.

## 8. Context, RAR, ARN, and Graphify

Build a small, provenance-rich **task context** only when needed: selected items and attachments, recent turn state, authorized source metadata/content, candidate IDs, and capability state. Graphify can point URI toward a source; URI must check that source and its permissions. RAR should bind a reference only to grounded candidates, preserving ambiguity. ARN.1â€™s verified narrowing applies to its current `NOT_FOUND` path; a future clarification renderer is separate proposed work despite the similar â€œARNâ€ name.

Before asking, URI may make a bounded read-only search through already-authorized evidence. Model-assisted comparison is permitted only for a qualified candidate-set task and must report inference as inference. For a low-consequence reversible action, URI may act on a sufficiently supported candidate while showing the selection and an easy correction. Consequential, external, destructive, or hard-to-reverse actions require clarification if identity remains unresolved.

A simple clarification can immediately say â€œWhich report do you mean?â€ with up to about four or five **grounded** selectable candidates, no padding, and a â€œNone of these / Enter something elseâ€ path. Selection binds a candidate ID; free input governs the next attempt. This user requirement **conflicts with M33.2â€™s accepted rule that visible confirmation wording be model-authored**. The future architecture revision must resolve that conflict explicitly. I recommend the bounded deterministic exception you specified, with Edge wording only when it measurably helps.

## 9â€“10. Native capability and residency

Available capability may exceed simultaneously resident capability. That is practical through installed on-demand models, but fast completion under switching pressure is **unproven on this machine**. Separate a provider/model registry from leases for resources URI owns. Track each leaseâ€™s ownership, placement, context/KV allocation, load state, observed memory, and reuse. Never infer permission to evict a model merely from seeing it in LM Studio or Ollama.

Compare permanent 9B residency, idle unload, cold demand load, Edge plus Main co-residency, CPU/GPU placement, and partial offload. The existing 9B run reached about 7.32 GB system GPU memory and 21.7 GB host RAM; that is reason to measure co-residency, not declare it impossible. The measured 6.08 s cold load makes demand loading a meaningful latency trade-off. Disk mapping and partial GPU offload are supported desktop mechanisms, but mapped weights still incur access and memory costs; the ESP32/TinyStories technique is not evidence that URI can cheaply stream a 9B model for every token. [LM Studio documents idle TTL and auto-evict behavior](https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/core/ttl-and-auto-evict); [llama.cpp documents loading and GPU layer placement](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md).

On the Ryzen 9 5900X, 24 GB RAM, RX 7900 GRE 16 GB, and Windows target, measure the **actual provider/backend** in use. Do not assume CUDA behavior or transfer a result from a different offload configuration. No always-resident 9B policy is ready to freeze.

## 11â€“12. Route learning and cost

Create a **separate per-user route-performance store** from URI knowledge and memory. A minimal record would hold task/capability class, qualified route and versions, context/provenance fingerprints, objective execution and task outcomes, explicit feedback if given, retries/escalation, latency and resources. Store raw conversation or correction text only when separately needed and governed; structured evidence is the default.

Durable learning defaults **ON** with ON/OFF, inspect, delete, and reset controls. OFF prevents new durable route/response-evaluation records while allowing normal operation and temporary task/session evidence, which is discarded when no longer needed. Resetting route preferences must not erase document knowledge.

Qualification is a hard eligibility gate. Within the **same independently qualified capability class**, accumulated evidence may gradually shift preference among routes. A routeâ€™s qualification, permission, safety requirement, or Edge/Capable boundary cannot be learned into existence. Weight negative feedback promptly; decay or invalidate evidence after model, tool, prompt, schema, qualification, or relevant context changes; reduce preference or roll back when measured quality deteriorates. Keep this inspectable and reversible.

Attach optional ðŸ‘, ðŸ‘Ž, and correction controls to the actual response/operation trace. Record technical execution, actual task completion, explicit acceptance, rejection, correction, and route performance separately. No response is a neutral signal. A â€œwrong referenceâ€ correction primarily examines context/RAR; poor wording examines drafting; a failed action examines tool binding and execution. One feedback item must not permanently change routing.

For each eligible route, estimate **end-to-end** cost: preparation + load/switch + inference + tools + expected retries + failure/escalation cost + resource pressure. Compare p50/p95 task completion and correctness by workload stratum; do not set an arbitrary universal millisecond target. The current route may be faster than a tiny-model chain that eventually calls the Main Brain anyway.

## 13â€“14. Failure, escalation, and hardware controls

Unknown task class, stale qualification, unsupported modality, missing evidence, resource denial, or failed bounded proposal should lead to an appropriate qualified route or an honest limitation. Do not retry a side effect without checking whether it executed. Preserve the action chain across local and cloud routes. Separate user permission to use a Brain from permission to perform an action.

The resource governor should budget at the shared **process** level, because concurrent users can compete for the same leases. It should measure CPU/RAM/VRAM where the runtime exposes them, context/KV growth, load/unload time, switching, queue delay, memory pressure, and coexistence. Missing telemetry is unknown, not spare capacity. The [M33.2 resource design](C:/Users/cheta/Development/Uri/_V1/docs/architecture/M33_2_EDGE_SECOND_BRAIN_CANONICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md) already defines lifecycle states and a shared pool; new work should extend and verify those contracts rather than duplicate them.

## 6. Outcome-oriented delegation: the Execution Capsule

URI delegates **bounded outcomes**. It does not micromanage harness actions. The capsule is URI-owned and harness-neutral:

| Field | Content | Source in URI |
|---|---|---|
| `objective` | What the user needs (Brain-formulated, re-evaluated) | canonical loop |
| `authoritative_references` | Resolved entities with binding tier (CONFIRMED / TENTATIVE) | RAR, D5 rule |
| `resources` | Staged files and workspace paths, with read or write scope | `file_store.py` (ADAPT) |
| `context` | Minimal relevant knowledge, preferences, prior evidence | capsule builder |
| `allowed_operations` | Toolsets and effect classes permitted | grants âˆ© mode âˆ© domain pack âˆ© posture |
| `prohibited_operations` | Explicit denials (for example send email, delete, submit) | policy |
| `brokered_tools` | URI MCP broker tools for consequential steps | broker |
| `expected_outcome` | Declarative end state | Brain + domain pack |
| `verification_criteria` | Checks URI will run itself | verifier |
| `budgets` | Time, tokens, cost, steps | usage ceilings |
| `intelligence` | Endpoint and model for the run | intelligence broker |
| `trace` | URI trace id | `uri_v1/evaluation` |

**Evaluation against real harnesses:**
- Hermes `/v1/runs` accepts `instructions` plus `model`, so the capsule maps onto instructions plus a pre-staged workspace plus a profile. Per-run toolsets were not found and are likely profile-level (VERIFIED, local source).
- Codex and ACP `session/prompt` take text plus a working directory.
- OpenHands takes a workspace plus a confirmation policy.

The capsule is therefore delivered as **(rendered instructions + staged workspace + harness profile + brokered MCP tools)**. No harness natively accepts structured verification criteria or prohibited-operation lists as enforced constraints. Enforcement comes from the profile, sandbox and broker, and **verification is URI's job**. The model is viable, with that caveat.
